scenario.title: People, organization roles and project permissions
situations: Add a teammate or change their authority.
A member can sign in but cannot act on a project.
Disable a person or retire a service identity.
scenario.current: Research trace; requirements and source paths need live proof.
questions: Trace each mode from no account to project access, including who can create project grants.
Check permission-denied responses for exact role/owner recovery without disclosure beyond authorized scope.

lessons.title: Separate person, membership, role and machine credential
lessons.when: Before granting access or explaining a permission refusal
lessons.need: Org roles admin/operator/viewer and project grants are distinct. Cloud membership/billing is platform-fed; machine-only service roles are not human roles. Machine admission does not automatically grant unrelated authority.
lessons.surface: Docs sidebar -> Actors/Members/Billing -> documented Actors and Machines surfaces.

lessons.title: Understand revocation and recovery
lessons.when: Before disabling an actor or changing the last admin
lessons.need: Disabling revokes keys and browser sessions; enabling does not restore keys. Last active admin and protected service identities have restrictions. Recover through the named authorized operation, then sign in/reconnect where necessary.
lessons.surface: Actors confirmation/role refusal documented in public guide; actor CLI help.

lessons.title: Find the add-person path in every mode
lessons.when: A new teammate needs initial access
lessons.need: Use the mode-appropriate invitation/account and machine admission route; do not give someone else an own-machine code or infer authority from an existing token.
lessons.surface: FIRST-USER item 33 proposes one simple add-people/machines route; public guide currently distinguishes Cloud Members and self-host machine authorization.
lessons.gap: Full invitation, project-grant creation and no-OIDC teammate flows were not traced. These are audit-needed, not claimed unsupported.
